static_traits.name: Lin Peilin
static_traits.family_status: Has a son who plays football
static_traits.medical_history: Denying major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, fairly cooperative; neutral attitude; able to describe troubles and tried strategies concretely

basic_info.main_problem: I often feel overwhelmed and stressed, because I believe I can never find time for personal interests (like reading mystery novels), since I must constantly drive my son to football training, games, and matches.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to find healthier coping to relieve stress and overwhelm, and to carve out reading time for myself under my son's busy football schedule.
growth_experiences: Since my son started playing football, stress gradually rose: initially moderate intensity, worsening as schedule demands increased; especially obvious when weekly activities are dense. She frequently handles pickups and dropoffs, feeling occupied by family responsibilities, finding it hard to reserve time for herself. Stress affects sleep and overall mood, occasionally losing temper at her son straining the relationship. Although her husband is supportive, she finds it hard to discuss this overwhelm and stress with him, worrying about burdening him.

core_beliefs: I am unable to control my own time and life
My needs are not important, family needs should come first

special_situations.event: The son has dense training, scrimmage, and match schedules within a week, requiring frequent pick-ups and drop-offs
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot arrange whole, continuous blocks of time for myself, it equals having no time, unable to pursue interests
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Prioritizes the son's schedule, continuously undertakes pick-up and drop-off tasks; tries time management and task prioritization to keep things running
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I never have my own time, I probably cannot read this new book at all

special_situations.event: Originally planned to read, but a new pick-up/drop-off need or a forgotten practice arrangement temporarily appeared, disrupting the plan
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once an emergency arises, all self-plans will fail, showing I am unable to carve out any time for myself
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Gives up communicating with the husband or seeking sharing, bears all pick-up and drop-off duties alone; reduces own activities to avoid plan frustration
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Things always happen, plans are meaningless

special_situations.event: Occasionally freeing a few minutes late at night but too tired to enjoy reading
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only reading in ample, continuous, high-quality time counts as effective; fragmented time is not worth it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating briefly usable time, avoiding fragmented reading attempts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: A few minutes are useless too, this does not count as truly my own time

special_situations.event: Thinking about discussing my overwhelm and stress with my husband
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Expressing personal needs would burden her husband; a 'good wife' should bear it herself
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repressing needs, not seeking help, staying silent to avoid troubling him
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not trouble him, he is busy too

core_conflict.wish: Longing for understood and supported personal space and time, to freely pursue interests (reading)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing expressing needs will burden family (especially husband), being judged selfish or causing relationship tension; also worrying family functioning will be affected
defense_goal: Maintaining family harmony and security by repressing self-needs and solely bearing caregiving and driving tasks

object_relations.self_representation: A caretaker/mother pressed breathless by family responsibilities
object_relations.object_representation: A high-need, time-consuming care recipient (the son)

object_relations.self_representation: A partner who should not trouble others
object_relations.object_representation: A busy but supportive husband, who may be burdened by her own needs

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing whether to express her stress and needs to her husband
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client subconsciously equates expressing needs with burdening her husband, worrying about being seen as selfish and rejected (transference)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a tactful, restrained tone, emphasizing the husband is busy and one should endure, avoiding directly making concrete requests or sharing plans

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes the behavioral experiment of 'setting aside 10 minutes for reading while the son practices'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing potential emergencies as inevitable, reinforcing anticipation of failure, thus keeping distance to avoid disappointment (transference)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a calm, pragmatic tone, raises hypothetical obstacles (for example 'inevitably will be interrupted'), uses many reasons to downplay the meaning of trying, while avoiding touching their own emotional needs

manifestations: As a full-time family caregiver, personal time is taken up by family responsibilities, making it hard to arrange reading time independently
Feeling 'swallowed up' by the schedule whenever the son's activities are dense
Finding it hard to discuss overwhelm and stress with husband, worrying about becoming his burden
Stays silent about personal needs in the family

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Believing 'a good wife should carry it alone', should not carve out time for oneself
Demanding of oneself not to trouble the husband

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not asking the husband for help, pushing the impulse to express needs back inward
Bears pick-up/drop-off tasks and care alone, sacrificing personal time

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Displacing focus with 'emergencies are inevitable' when discussing feasible plans, avoiding implementing concrete arrangements
Emphasizing uncertainty in a doubtful tone, reducing positive exploration

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Believing 'I should not trouble him', excessively restraining expression of self-needs
Self-limiting out of worry about burdening others

positive_force: The husband has a supportive attitude (though not yet fully communicated)
Willing to try behavioral experiments and accept the strategy of 'starting small'
Able to identify potential time windows (early morning, during son's practice)
Highly devoted to family responsibilities, strong action ability (continuously completes pick-ups/drop-offs and coordination)
negative_force: Catastrophic and overgeneralized thinking ('things always happen, plans are meaningless')
Negating positive cues and black-and-white standards (seeing fragmented time as 'useless')
Avoids expressing needs, finds it hard to seek support (communication with the husband is blocked)
Sleep disturbance and low mood leading to insufficient energy and declining patience

target_behavior.behavior: High-intensity stress and irritability appearing when the son's soccer activities are dense (emotional reactions)
antecedent: When the son's weekly training, scrimmages, and matches are densely scheduled
Last-minute added pickup tasks or forgotten activity arrangements
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic and overgeneralized cognition about losing personal time (believing 'never have time')
target_behavior.function: Evades guilt related to expressing one's needs and potential family conflict, maintains family functioning
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep disturbance, low mood, tense relationship with son, overall decline in sense of well-being

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids expressing needs to the husband and seeking sharing of burdens (communication avoidance)
antecedent: Thinking about discussing overwhelm and stress with the husband
When situations requiring fighting for one's own time arise
target_behavior.core_reason: Worries about adding burden to the husband, being judged as selfish, or triggering conflict
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible negative evaluation and relationship tension, maintaining surface harmony
target_behavior.consequence: Bears all transport and care tasks alone, personal time further compressed, stress intensifies
